newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bavaria's Stoiber moots shorter EMU transition.
newsitem.headline: Bavaria's Stoiber moots shorter EMU transition.

text.p: Bavarian state premier Edmund Stoiber, a leading German hard-liner on the criteria for entry into Europe's single currency, on Saturday proposed shortening the transition period for the completion of monetary union.

In a summary of a television interview to be shown later in the day, Stoiber was quoted as saying that such a move should be considered if it looked as if countries might fail the entry criteria for Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).

"Cutting the conversion time (to full replacement of national currencies by the euro) would be a realistic scenario," Stoiber said according to a summary of his comments released by the N-TV commercial television station.
At present, it is planned that the currency exchange rates of EMU participants will be irrevocably locked and European monetary policy will be carried out in euros on January 1, 1999.
The full replacement of all participating national currencies by the euro must then happen by January 1, 2002, three years later.
Stoiber said the transition period could be cut to two years and still hit the 2002 start date. That would mean that the locking-in of exchange rates need only occur in 2000.
Stoiber further repeated demands that the euro should be as strong a currency as the deutschemark.
